newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin hands resignation to prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin hands resignation to prime minister.

text.p: Embattled Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan on Thursday handed his resignation to Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, a government official said.
"Amnuay has submitted his resignation letter to the prime minister," Sornchai Montriwat, deputy secretary general to the prime minister for political affairs, told reporters.

Separately, Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee who was chosen by Amnuay to be part of his economic team, said he would resign along with the finance minister. "I can confirm that I will resign although I have not submitted my letter which I expect to do by this weekend," Narongchai said.

Amnuay told reporters after meeting premier Chavalit Yongchaiyudh that his departure would not lead to major changes in the government's approach to managing the Thai economy, which is going through its worst period in over a decade.
Political sources said Amnuay's resignation was triggered by rifts between him and political rivals from within Chavalit's six-party coalition government over his handling of the ailing economy.

Amnuay became finance minister in December when the Chavalit administration rose to power through a general election. Analysts expect his departure to cause more problems for the Thai economy as a suitable successor would not be easy to find.
